clue.text: Clothing valets vow to get together

parts.note: valets are manservants, so men
to vow is to swear

explanation.surface: Gentlemen's gentlemen solemnly pledge to meet up.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments made for males are a shop's clothing department, a general name for such garments.

clue.text: Society member cooked outside rear of canteen

indicators.note: the cooked word sits around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: fried is one way food is cooked

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, here of canteen

explanation.surface: A club member was cooked up outside the back of the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Society is the Religious Society of Friends, whose members are Quakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Quaker belongs to the Religious Society of Friends, hence a member is called by that name.

clue.text: Nervous person in a hide, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: someone jittery who fidgets and jerks
a birdwatcher, who sits concealed in a hide waiting to spot rare birds

explanation.surface: An anxious type hiding away somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a keen birdwatcher chasing rare sightings is called by this name; a hide is a shelter for watching birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a jumpy fidgeter and an avid British birdwatcher are described with this word.

clue.text: Search for groom?

definitions.meaning: to search thoroughly, as when going over an area
to tidy hair with a toothed tool

explanation.surface: Looking for a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both meticulous searching and grooming hair with a toothed implement.

clue.text: First of schoolboys, crazy and covered in zits

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of schoolboys

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A schoolboy at the front of the class, mad and pimply.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin marked by many pimples is described as having spots, a common British adjective.

clue.text: Ruin university don originally in Japanese drama

indicators.note: the letter from don goes inside the drama's name

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese masked theatre

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of don

explanation.surface: An academic ruined by appearing in a Japanese play.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin someone is to bring about their downfall, the old sense of reversing their fortunes.

clue.text: Tolerate bad-mannered fellow

definitions.meaning: to put up with or endure
a gruff, rude man, likened to the animal

explanation.surface: Putting up with a rude man.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means endure; the noun is a surly, uncouth person compared to the grizzly animal.

clue.text: Enormous place where the Times is produced, it's said

indicators.note: signals a word heard rather than read: the place name is spoken

parts.words: place where the Times is produced
parts.note: Wapping in east London is where The Times was famously printed

explanation.surface: A huge printing site for The Times newspaper, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: WAPPING is a district of east London long associated with The Times newspaper's printing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally something huge or massive is described with this slangy intensifier.

clue.text: Very little money to cover son's climb

indicators.note: the money phrase wraps around the son, covering him

parts.note: a cent is a tiny coin, so a cent is very little money
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: Barely any cash to fund a boy's climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb up a slope or mountain is a rise, also named with this noun.

clue.text: Period of prosperity embracing abstinent weaver

indicators.note: the boom wraps around the abstinent letters

parts.note: an economic boom is a time of prosperity
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A boom time hugging a teetotal textile worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The weaver is Nick Bottom in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Nick of this name is a weaver by trade in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: It has legal force, whichever way you look at it

definitions.note: a signed legal document carries binding force in law; the same letters read in either direction

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the word reads the same from either end, so both directions give it

parts.note: a signed legal document carries binding force in law; the same letters read in either direction

explanation.surface: Something legally binding however you view it.
explanation.definitionFit: A signed legal document such as a conveyance carries binding force in law.

clue.text: Insect: one unknown in Hebe's recollection

indicators.note: the inserted pieces go into the rearranged name
re-collection: the letters of Hebe are gathered again in a new order

parts.note: the goddess's name, the 's simply possessive
taken as written
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An insect sting remembered by the goddess Hebe.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth; 'recollection' is read as re-collection, gathering her letters again in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey-making bee is a familiar species of insect, the hive-dwelling kind.

clue.text: Failure to employ socially unacceptable pundit

parts.note: non-U is a British term for not upper-class, socially unacceptable
a pundit is an expert or wise person, a sage

explanation.surface: Not hiring a commentator because they are socially unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class and not upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of use of something, failing to put it to work, is this rare noun.

clue.text: Odd lore circulating around a place of riches

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the a
the letters of odd lore move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Strange legends circulating about a fabled wealthy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' rearranges ODDLORE into ELDORDO, and 'around' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary South American city of gold stands for any fabulously wealthy place.

clue.text: Irish island group served by neat vessel

indicators.note: the island group comes after neat, being served by it

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy
the Aran Islands lie off Galway in Ireland

explanation.surface: Islands off Ireland served by a tidy boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat with three parallel hulls is a type of sailing vessel.

clue.text: Importance blokes recognised in vehicle test

indicators.note: the blokes are found inside the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Men noticed something significant during a car test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the annual British roadworthiness check for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of great significance are said to be of great weight, as in 'of moment'.

clue.text: Ordered to be naughty, some say?

indicators.note: some speakers pronounce the word so it is heard like the naughty one

parts.note: bad means naughty, as of a child

explanation.surface: Told to misbehave, according to some people.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bid: to command someone is to have bid them do it.

clue.text: Unusually large car part

definitions.meaning: as in a ... harvest, exceptionally big
the protective bar at front and rear of a car

explanation.surface: An oversized automobile component.
explanation.definitionFit: An exceptionally big crop is called this, and so is the impact bar on a car.

clue.text: Household attendant from the old sultanate

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A servant from an ancient Arabian sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a servant or retainer in a noble or royal household bore this title.

clue.text: Made-up name for dairy product

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the whole word Made, read as written; that it sits in Made-up is no hidden word but a coincidence of the hyphen, with up the indicator

explanation.surface: An invented brand name for a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese in a red wax coat is a dairy product.

clue.text: Fixer we have at our fingertips?

definitions.meaning: something that fastens, as a pin hammered into wood
the horny plate at the end of each finger

explanation.surface: A fixer always close to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the metal pin for fastening and the keratin plate on a fingertip share this name.

clue.text: Cross about doctor being so gloomy?

indicators.note: the annoyed word wraps around the doctor

parts.note: cross means annoyed, sore
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Is an angry doctor this downcast?
explanation.definitionFit: Dark and melancholy in mood or colour, synonymous with dismal.

clue.text: Unforgettable article going into country pursuit

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the pursuit

parts.note: hunting with hounds is a traditional British country pursuit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A memorable piece written about country sports.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody that lingers in the memory is described as staying with you, recurring.

clue.text: Donkey loses head in whirlpool

indicators.note: the donkey word drops its opening letter

parts.note: neddy is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey decapitated in a swirling current.
explanation.definitionFit: A small swirl of water moving in a circle is a whirlpool in miniature.
